reason: Both correctly identified an iced evaporator from a failing defrost system and recommended a 24h manual defrost, but Conversation 2 then asked the homeowner to remove the inner freezer back panel to expose the coils, which crosses the stated safety boundary (evaporator cover removal is engineer work), while Conversation 1 explicitly warned against chipping ice or using a hairdryer, covered food safety, and kept all checks within the homeowner's remit. Conversation 1 also pre-empted the full decision tree in fewer turns - 'if it returns in days, the defrost heater/sensor/control is failing, get a technician, check warranty' - whereas Conversation 2 took many single-question turns and only escalated at the end. Conversation 2 does earn credit for reaching a clean, correct engineer referral after recurrence, and Conversation 1's opening generic checklist with US units was weaker, but neither named an unsupported part and Conversation 1's safer, more complete guidance wins.
